answer: One meadow plot per identity anchors a pulse-meter bond: claimant locks a 70-credit bond, registers a plot with a key-bound pulse meter, and files a pulse rate. A meter log records pulses, and a meadow auditor computes the delta between claim and metered rate; beyond 3 percent the bond burns and the claim voids. Fees rise: first 34, kth 34+6(k-1), 1000th 6028, so 1000 fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 70,000 bond. A rented-meter ring fails because one meter key cannot serve two plots, and duplicate logs burn bonds. An honest claimant pays 34 once and recovers the bond after audit.
